description:
Looking for an opportunity to make an impact? 
 At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainably. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. Our Mission, Vision, and Values guide the way we do business.

 Are you ready for your next challenge?  
 Within the Defense Sector, Leidos currently has an opening for a talented Software Engineer to work onsite in our Huntsville, AL office in support of the IFPC program, developing software for critical counter-UAS and missile defense solutions. This position focuses on the complete software lifecycle of complex defense systems in a Linux environment using languages such as C++ and Python, developed within a Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) environment.
  
 What’s in it for you? 
 This is a high-impact, hands-on technical role. You will work alongside the team’s technical lead as a builder of AI-assisted engineering tooling, helping put modern, agentic AI coding practices into practice on the program while also delivering mission software. The ideal candidate has built working software with current-generation AI coding assistants and is excited to help adapt those practices to a secure environment where the newest commercial tooling is often restricted.

 THE CHALLENGE (primary responsibilities) 
 Partner closely with the team’s technical lead to translate the team’s AI-assisted development strategy into working tools, workflows, and practices.
 Design, build, and maintain AI-assisted development tooling, including custom agents/skills, prompt libraries, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, and automated AI code-review and test-generation pipelines.
 Support team adoption of AI coding assistants by pairing with engineers, answering day-to-day questions, and contributing to playbooks and enablement materials.
 Help stand up and maintain on-prem / self-hosted model environments (e.g., vLLM, Ollama) for secure, restricted, or air-gapped use, and prepare technical documentation that supports the security approval of AI tooling.
 Develop production software in C++ and Python in a Linux environment for counter-UAS and missile defense systems.
 Develop within a SAFe environment using Jira and GitLab; apply software best practices such as peer reviews, unit testing, and CI/CD automation – integrating AI responsibly into the software development lifecycle.
 Debug and troubleshoot software in a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL) and Software-in-the-Loop (SWIL) setting.
 Follow and help refine team engineering and coding standards, and produce standardized, reusable, well-documented solutions.
 Collaborate with systems, electrical, test, and cybersecurity engineers to integrate AI tooling and deliver mission software.
 
 WHAT SETS YOU APART (basic qualifications) 
 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline and 4+ years of professional software development experience (or Master’s degree + 2 years).
 Hands-on experience using AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor) to build working software in professional, academic, or personal projects.
 Proficiency in C++ or Python, with working knowledge of the other.
 Experience across the software lifecycle, including peer reviews, automated testing, and CI/CD.
 Experience developing in a Linux environment.
 Currently living in Huntsville, AL or willing to relocate.
 Candidate must be a U.S. Citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret Security Clearance (interim and final).
  
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Deep, hands-on experience with specific agentic AI coding tools – e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot / Copilot Workspace, Windsurf, Aider.
 Experience building MCP servers, custom agents/skills, prompt/agent libraries, or AI-integrated CI pipelines (e.g., automated code review or test generation).
 Experience deploying or operating self-hosted / on-prem large language models and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over codebases (e.g., vLLM, Ollama, Amazon Bedrock / GovCloud), including in disconnected environments.
 Experience adapting modern AI-assisted development workflows to security-constrained, restricted, or disconnected environments.
 Python scripting and automation experience for developer tooling and productivity.
 Experience coaching or mentoring other engineers, including helping peers adopt new tools or practices.
 Familiarity with AI governance and safety for software teams: secure use of AI on sensitive code, data-handling, and intellectual-property and security guardrails.
 Commercial / private-sector software experience where access to state-of-the-art agentic AI coding tools is widespread.
 Experience working within an Agile / SAFe environment and with tools such as Jira and GitLab (or equivalent).
 Counter-UAS, missile defense, or other mission-system domain experience.
 Real-time / embedded C++ and experience troubleshooting/testing software in an HWIL environment.
 Experience with Buildroot and VMware; network programming (UDP/TCP) and analysis tools such as Wireshark.
 Experience supporting and maintaining CI/CD pipelines.
 If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.
 
 
 Original Posting: 
November 23, 2026 
 For U.S. Positions: While subject to change based on business needs, Leidos reasonably anticipates that this job requisition will remain open for at least 3 days with an anticipated close date of no earlier than 3 days after the original posting date as listed above.







 
 
 Pay Range: 
Pay Range $87,100.00 - $157,450.00 
 The Leidos pay range for this job level is a general guideline only and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, applicable bargaining agreement (if any), or other law.
